verified.name: Structured3D
verified.pairing: 3,500 professional designer CAD house models (21,835 rooms, from Kujiale) — SAME design as: (a) full structured 3D annotation (planes/lines/junctions with per-plane semantics incl. door and window openings, room layouts, floorplan), (b) furniture 3D bounding boxes, (c) 196,515 photorealistic panoramic + perspective renders under full/simple/empty furniture configs with semantic/depth/normal/albedo GT. 2D floor plan is directly derivable from the 3D primitive annotation — a true same-design 2D↔3D pair.
verified.availability: Free for research after signing an agreement form (Structured3D Terms of Use); download granted manually. Code MIT. Size undisclosed on page; multi-part, hundreds of GB for full renders. Mirror seen on HuggingFace (Gen3DF/Structured3D).
verified.relevance: F1: furniture 3D boxes give identity GT visible in the paired render; F2: box orientation in 3D vs symbol in derived plan; F3: room-type semantics (16 types); F4: doors/windows are explicit 3D openings (no hinged-vs-sliding subtype); F5: weak (scenes mostly single-storey). Best single synthetic backbone for render-as-ground-truth backwards learning.
verified.semantic_labels: Per-plane semantics (wall/door/window/floor/ceiling), 16 room types, junction/line wireframe, furniture 3D bboxes, per-pixel semantic + depth + normal in renders. No door-type (sliding) subtype, no explicit indoor/outdoor flag.

verify.evidence: PAIRING — largely CONFIRMED. Paper (arXiv 1908.00222 / ECCV'20, ar5iv full text): "3,500 scenes (i.e., houses)" with "21,835 rooms" and 196,515 photo-realistic renderings (Table 1; abstract says "more than 196k"); designs "created by professional designers"; GitHub README acknowledges "Kujiale.com for providing the database of house designs and the rendering engine". annotation_3d.json (data_organization.md) contains junctions (3D coords), lines (point+direction), planes (type/normal/offset), plus "semantics" mapping type = room type / door / window to planeIDs, planeLineMatrix, lineJunctionMatrix, cuboids, manhattan. Furniture 3D bboxes confirmed: per-scene bbox_3d.json (basis rotation matrix / coeffs / centroid, SUN RGB-D format; added 2019-10-16). Floorplan derivability explicitly CONFIRMED in the paper: "identify all lines in L and junction points in X which lie on a 'floor'... and project all 'rooms', 'doors', and 'windows' to this floor" to obtain a vector floorplan; repo ships visualize_floorplan.py. GT modalities per render confirmed: semantic (NYUv2 40-label), instance (16-bit, full config only), albedo, depth (millimeters), normal, plus layout.txt/layout.json; panorama RGB in 3 lighting variants (raw/cold/warm). Resolutions 512x1024 pano, 720x1280 perspective. LABELS — CONFIRMED with one nuance: plane "type" field is only ceiling/floor/wall; door/window arrive via the separate semantics-to-planeID mapping ("'door' or 'window' is an opening which connects two rooms"), so "per-plane semantics incl. door/window" is functionally right. Room types = exactly 16, verbatim from metadata/room_types.txt: living room, kitchen, bedroom, bathroom, balcony, corridor, dining room, study, studio, store room, garden, laundry room, office, basement, garage, undefined. No sliding-door subtype and no indoor/outdoor flag anywhere in data_organization.md (word "outwall" absent); only weak outdoor signal is room types "balcony"/"garden". AVAILABILITY — mostly confirmed: site + README: "To download the dataset, please fill the agreement form that indicates you agree to the Structured3D Terms of Use"; ToU = non-commercial research and educational purposes only, no redistribution, citation required; "the code is released under the MIT license"; no dataset size stated on site/README/paper; distribution is multi-part zips (Structured3D_0.zip, Structured3D_1.zip, ...).
verify.corrections: Three inaccuracies/unverified details: (1) Furniture configs: full/simple/empty applies to PANORAMAS only; perspective renders come in empty/full configs only (data_organization.md: panorama/<empty|simple|full> vs perspective/<empty|full>) — claim overstates "full/simple/empty" for both. Other HF derivatives exist (Pointcept/structured3d-compressed, 3dlg-hcvc/structured3d-arch), likewise not full mirrors. (3) "Hundreds of GB for full renders" and "download granted manually" could not be verified from any fetched page — multi-part zips confirmed, total size undisclosed everywhere; treat the size figure as unsourced. Minor wording nuance: door/window are opening semantics mapped to plane IDs, not values of the plane "type" field (which is only ceiling/floor/wall).

verified.size: ~6.8K houses, 18K+ furnished rooms, 3D-FUTURE ~10-16K textured models (tens of GB)

verified.name: Aria Synthetic Environments (SceneScript, Meta)
verified.pairing: 100K procedurally generated furnished apartments: each scene = 3D floor plan expressed in SceneScript/ASE Scene Language (CAD-like commands: feature TYPE, location, dimensions for walls/doors/windows/pillars) PAIRED with photorealistic egocentric walkthrough video + depth + instance segmentation (58M+ images) + object classes. The 'plan as language' side is a machine-readable symbolic twin of the 3D render side.
verified.availability: Public for research under Project Aria dataset license (non-commercial); download via aria_synthetic_environments_downloader / HuggingFace. Full set ~23TB (per-scene subsets feasible).
verified.relevance: F2: object instances + trajectories; F4: doors/windows are first-class typed-by-kind (not sliding-vs-hinged) parametric tokens — a good schema model for our own 'plan language'; F1: instance-to-class maps; F3/F5: not covered (single-storey apartments). Procedural, not designer-authored — weaker symbol realism than Structured3D/3D-FRONT.
verified.semantic_labels: SceneScript commands (make_wall/make_door/make_window with dimensions), 2D instance→class mappings, depth, 6DoF trajectory.

verify.evidence: All three parts check out across the official docs page, the arXiv abstract, the HuggingFace page, the download docs, and the license page. PAIRING: docs page states "100,000 unique multi-room interior scenes" with ~2-minute egocentric trajectories, "58M+" images, "~23TB" total; per scene: simulated Aria RGB stream, "2D depth map", "2D instance segmentation" with per-scene object class mappings, "6DoF camera trajectory", and a "3D floor plan" in "ASE Scene Language" — described verbatim as architectural features "such as doors, windows and pillars, described with a CAD-like language that includes the feature type, location and dimensions". arXiv 2403.13064 abstract confirms: "SceneScript... produces full scene models as a sequence of structured language commands" and "we generate and release a large-scale synthetic dataset called Aria Synthetic Environments consisting of 100k high-quality in-door scenes, with photorealistic and ground-truth annotated renders of egocentric scene walkthroughs." LABELS: the ase_data_format page lists per-scene files ase_scene_language.txt, rgb/ (10 FPS fisheye JPEG), depth/ (16-bit PNG, mm), instances/ (16-bit segmentation PNG), trajectory.txt (GT poses), object_instances_to_classes.json, plus semidense point clouds; and names the exact commands: "make_wall - the full set of parameters specifies a gravity-aligned oriented box", "make_door - specify box-based cutouts from walls", "make_window - specify box-based cutouts from wall". AVAILABILITY: download docs state "By downloading the datasets you agree that you have read and accepted the terms of the Aria Synthetic Environments Dataset License Agreement" (projectaria.com/datasets/ase/license/), which restricts use to non-commercial research (scene understanding, scene reconstruction, camera localization & mapping, etc.); download is via the aria_synthetic_environments_downloader script with per-scene subsets supported via a --scene-ids range parameter (e.g., scenes 0-9 or 560-569), so per-scene subsets of the ~23TB set are feasible as claimed. The HuggingFace page projectaria/aria-synthetic-environments exists and cites the same license and paper.

verified.name: Zillow Indoor Dataset (ZInD)
verified.pairing: REAL homes: 1,575 unfurnished US residences, 67,448 360° panoramas (33,210 primary + 34,238 secondary) localized against annotated 3D room layouts and final 2D floor plans of the SAME home — the largest real plan↔3D-capture pairing. 19,403 windows + 48,759 doors annotated.
verified.availability: Academic use only, explicitly not licensed for commercial purposes; register on Zillow Bridge Platform + ~500-word research proposal to ZInD@zillowgroup.com, manual approval up to 2 weeks; ~40GB via download_data.py. Code Apache-2.0.
verified.relevance: F4: real-world W/D/O taxonomy distinguishes window vs door vs OPENING (doorless passage) with positions on both pano and plan — the exact 'what did the drafter mean at this wall gap' supervision, though door types (sliding/hinged) are NOT distinguished; F3: layouts follow real Manhattan/non-Manhattan distributions, panoramas show glassed vs open boundaries the plan flattens; F5: multi-floor homes have per-floor plans + panos (trees visible through glass in panos but absent from plans = natural F5 negative evidence). F1/F2: nil — homes are unfurnished.
verified.semantic_labels: Room layouts (3D polygons), W/D/O 2D boxes on panos + plan, room labels, camera poses; no furniture, no door subtypes.

verify.evidence: GitHub README (github.com/zillow/zind, verified via repo page + raw README.md, main branch) confirms nearly everything: "ZInD is an RGB 360º panoramas dataset containing 67,448 panoramas taken in 1,575 unfurnished residential homes, annotated with 3D room layouts, 2D bounding boxes for W/D/O, merged room layouts, 3D camera poses, and final 2D floor plans." Stats table verbatim: "# panoramas (pri) | 33210", "# panoramas (sec) | 34238" (sum = 67,448), "# floor plans | 2737", "# rooms | 22484", "# windows | 19403", "# doors | 48759". US: "photographers across 20 US cities and 12 states were hired to do the capture." Secondary panos "are localized within room layouts using a semi-automatic approach" and data_organization.md gives per-pano `floor_plan_transformation` (translation/rotation/scale) — supports "localized against layouts + final 2D floor plans of the SAME home". Room labels confirmed in data_organization.md: "label | Subfield within the panorama field containing the label of the room, e.g., 'kitchen'." W/D/O stored as "2D bounding boxes for windows, doors and openings in local coordinates" inside each panorama's layout_raw/complete/visible. No furniture annotations and no door subtypes appear anywhere in the docs (homes are unfurnished), consistent with the claim's negatives. Availability: README verbatim "Zillow licenses ZInD for academic use only. ZInD is **not** licensed for commercial purposes"; register on Bridge Platform + agree to Zillow Data Terms of Use; "The decision to approve or deny the request may take up to two weeks"; size "about 40GB" via download_data.py; "code is released under the Apache License". The "largest" superlative traces to the CVPR 2021 paper abstract (via search snippets — CVF openaccess PDF/HTML and IEEE both 403'd direct fetch): "ZInD is the largest real dataset with layout annotations" — note the PAPER abstract cites 71,474 panoramas from 1,524 homes (pre-release numbers), while the released dataset README says 67,448/1,575. The W/D/O background blog URL (zillow.com/tech/training-models-to-detect-windows-doors-in-panos/) returned HTTP 403 on 2 attempts (Zillow blocks the fetcher); could not verify its content, but the W/D/O counts are independently in the README.
verify.corrections: Two nuances keep this at partial. (1) ACCESS FLOW conflated: the ~500-word proposal is NOT part of the standard academic registration. Per README, academic users with verifiable institutional credentials/institutional email simply register on the Bridge Platform and wait for manual approval (up to two weeks); only researchers NOT affiliated with a university/research institute must first email ZInD@zillowgroup.com with "a proposal (500 words minimum)". Also it is "500 words minimum", not "~500-word". (2) "Largest real plan↔3D-capture pairing" is a paraphrase of the 2021 paper's claim "largest real dataset with layout annotations" (a 2021-era claim, absent from the README; the paper abstract's own counts are 71,474 panos/1,524 homes vs the released 67,448/1,575). Minor label nuance: W/D/O boxes are 2D bounding boxes in the room-layout's local (floor-plan) coordinates attached to each panorama's layout, not pixel boxes drawn on the equirectangular image — "on panos + plan" is approximately right but loose. Openings are annotated too but the README gives no opening count and notes openings "are later processed for removal" in merged geometry. Everything else in PAIRING/LABELS/AVAILABILITY is confirmed verbatim, including 1,575 unfurnished US homes, 33,210+34,238=67,448 panos, 19,403 windows, 48,759 doors, room labels, camera poses, no furniture/door subtypes, academic-only license, Bridge Platform, ~40GB via download_data.py, code Apache-2.0.

verified.name: LIFULL HOME'S Dataset (NII IDR, Japan)
verified.pairing: REAL Japanese rental listings: 5.33M listings with floor-plan image + room PHOTOS of the SAME unit (83M images total, plus 5.31M high-res floor plan images) + structured listing metadata (area, layout type, facilities). The plan and the photos are the same design — the largest real 2D-plan↔photo pairing in existence. (The Raster-to-Vector/R2V 870-plan vector annotations derive from this corpus.)
verified.availability: Free for research via application to NII Informatics Research Data Repository (institutional research agreement; provided to 80+ labs incl. overseas). ~1.6GB TSV + ~210GB images + ~140GB hi-res plans. Photos are small (max 120x120 in the bulk set).
verified.relevance: F1: photo of the room verifies what each plan symbol is; F3: balconies/engawa visible in photos vs plan; F4: sliding doors are ubiquitous in Japanese housing and drawn with distinct conventions — photos disambiguate them (no explicit labels, backwards-learning needed); F5: multi-storey plans present. Asian drawing conventions = closest public analog to Thai residential PDFs.
verified.semantic_labels: No vector semantics in the bulk set (raster plans + photos + listing metadata); semantic GT must be minted by pairing, which is exactly the backwards-learning play.

verify.evidence: URL is live (NII IDR English page, https://www.nii.ac.jp/dsc/idr/en/lifull/). Confirmed on-page: Snapshot Data of Rentals (2015-09) = "5.33 million" listings all over Japan; "Image data (83 million files): floor plan image, room view, etc. of all the above items; approx. 210GB .jpg format files, max size: 120x120"; "High resolution version data of floor plan image (5.31 million files) included in Snapshot Data of Rentals; approx. 140GB .jpg"; Snapshot TSV "approx. 1.6GB"; metadata = "rental fee, area, location, age, floor plan, structure, facilities, etc."; "available free of charge", "Only researchers belonging to a university or a public research institution can apply", organization-level signed Consent Form required, "Overseas distribution began. (2020/09/07)". Pairing per unit: the EN page says images are "of all the above items" (the listings), and the NII IDR user-forum poster (nii.ac.jp/dsc/idr/userforum/poster/IDR-UF2023_LIFULL.pdf, read in full) states the images are 「上記に紐付く画像データ 物件画像（8300万点）間取り図（515万点）」 — i.e., property photos AND floor-plan images linked to the same listing records; the same poster showcases Liu/Wu/Kohli/Furukawa "Deep Multi-Modal Image Correspondence Learning" (arXiv:1612.01225) learning floor-plan↔room-photo correspondence on this data, and explicitly cites Raster-to-Vector (Liu et al., ICCV 2017) as structure analysis done on this dataset's floor plans; external sources (R2V paper/GitHub art-programmer/FloorplanTransformation) confirm 870 annotated floorplans derived from LIFULL HOME'S, annotations shareable but raster images not. LABELS claim consistent: bulk set is raster JPEG + TSV; no vector/semantic annotations mentioned anywhere on the NII pages (only per-image TYPE tags like 玄関/キッチン plus free-text captions — a small extra beyond the claim's "no semantics"). Also on-page but omitted by the claim: newer Posting Period Data 2018-10..2024-03 (9.28M rentals + 0.77M sales, ~2.6GB TSV, ~10GB high-res images) added 2025-05-27.
verify.corrections: Two parts are not supported by the cited page: (1) "provided to 80+ labs incl. overseas" — no user count appears on any NII IDR page; corroboration exists only in LIFULL's own materials (Kiyota's Speaker Deck "Past and Future of the LIFULL HOME'S Data Set": applications exceeded 100 by Oct 2019, incl. Japan/US/Canada/China), so the figure is if anything understated but should be cited to LIFULL's deck, not the NII page; note NII formally began overseas distribution 2020-09-07. (2) "the largest real 2D-plan↔photo pairing in existence" — a superlative nowhere claimed on the page; plausible but unverifiable. Minor numeric wrinkle: the English page says 5.31M high-res floor plans, but the Japanese page (nii.ac.jp/dsc/idr/lifull/homes.html) and the LIFULL poster say 約515万 (5.15M) — NII's own EN/JP pages disagree; the claim matches the EN figure. Also, eligibility is slightly narrower than "free for research": academic research in informatics-related fields, university/public research institutions only (companies excluded), and the high-res floor-plan set requires a separate application. verified.name: Rent3D++ (Plan2Scene, CVPR 2021) / Rent3D
verified.pairing: REAL London apartments: 215 units with floor plan + interior photos of the same residence; Rent3D++ adds corrected room categories, wall outlines, room-photo assignment, rectified surface crops, and 3D mesh generation code (plan→textured 3D mesh). Small but fully curated real 2D↔photo↔3D pipeline.
verified.availability: Download via Google Form on the project page (research use; inherits Rent3D/LIFULL-style listing-image provenance). Code public on GitHub (3dlg-hcvc/plan2scene).
verified.relevance: F3 is the standout: room category set explicitly includes outdoor, balcony, terrace vs indoor types — labeled indoor/outdoor zoning on real plans; F1: photos verify symbols; F4: photos show glazed boundaries. Tiny (215 units) — benchmark, not training corpus.
verified.semantic_labels: Room categories incl. {outdoor, balcony, terrace, closet, corridor, staircase...}, wall outlines, photo→room assignment.

verify.evidence: PROJECT PAGE (https://3dlg-hcvc.github.io/plan2scene/): presents Plan2Scene (CVPR 2021) as "Converting Floorplan to 3D Scenes" producing "a textured 3D mesh model"; dataset = Rent3D++, "a dataset of floorplans and photos from prior work" augmented "with rectified surface crops and additional annotations"; "Download Dataset" links Google Form https://forms.gle/mKAmnrzAm3LCK9ua6; source code linked on GitHub at 3dlg-hcvc/plan2scene. verified.name: FloorPlanCAD (ICCV 2021)
verified.pairing: 15,663 REAL CAD drawings (residential + commercial) as SVG VECTOR graphics with LINE-GRAINED panoptic annotation + 1000x1000 PNG rasters. Not 2D↔3D, but 2D-symbol↔semantic-truth at the primitive level — the direct codification of what CAD symbols mean.
verified.availability: CC BY-NC 4.0. Original project site discontinued 2022; dataset alive on HuggingFace (load_from_hub('Voxel51/FloorPlanCAD') via FiftyOne). Splits 6,382 train / 3,712 test.
verified.relevance: THE F4 source: explicit door taxonomy {single door, double door, SLIDING DOOR} + window taxonomy {window, bay window, blind window, opening symbol} as vector line-groups — the only public dataset that types sliding doors; F1: furniture symbol classes (sofa, bed, chair, table, bedside cupboard, TV cabinet, wardrobe, sink, bath, gas stove, refrigerator, washing machine...) annotated per line — exactly the desk-vs-cabinet confusion class list; F2/F3/F5: no.
verified.semantic_labels: 35 categories (30 things + 5 stuff incl. wall, parking): 3 door types incl. sliding, 4 window types, stairs, appliances, furniture, sanitary; per-primitive (line) instance+semantic labels.

verified.name: Raster-to-Vector: Revisiting Floorplan Transformation (Liu et al., ICCV 2017) + R2V/LIFULL data
verified.pairing: 2D raster plan image -> 2D vector-graphics plan of the SAME design (junction graph + per-pixel semantics + icon boxes); authors also released 100k+ machine-generated vector plans. No 3D artifact; this is the canonical raster->vector semantics stage that 3D lifters (e.g., Plan2Scene) consume.
verified.availability: MIT code; pretrained Torch7 AND PyTorch weights on Google Drive; hand-annotated vector ground truth released; underlying LIFULL raster images restricted (Japanese national-institute agreement).
verified.relevance: F1: icons are detected as class-labeled boxes, then a final INTEGER PROGRAMMING step enforces global topological consistency (loop closure, openings must lie on walls) — semantics is repaired by a deterministic global gate, not by the network; template for our placement gate. F4: doors/windows are represented ONLY as line segments attached to walls ('openings'); there is no glass/curtain-wall class at all — thin-line glass is representationally invisible in this lineage.
verified.semantic_labels: 13 junction types; wall segments; wall-attached opening segments (door/window not differentiated in geometry stage); icon classes (toilet, bathtub, sink, cooking counter, washing basin, entrance, closet, 'special'); per-pixel room-type labels.
verified.size: ~870 manually annotated plans + 100,000+ auto-vectorized plans; ~90% junction precision/recall reported

verify.evidence: PAIRING — largely CONFIRMED. Paper (ICCV 2017, read in full from downloaded PDF): input = rasterized floorplan image; a CNN produces a "junction layer" ("a set of junctions (i.e., points with types) or per-pixel semantic classification scores"), integer programming aggregates junctions into primitives ("wall lines, door lines, or icon boxes"), post-processing yields the final vector format of the same plan. 100k+ machine-generated vector plans: README links "100,000+ vector-graphics representation generated by our algorithm" on Google Drive; paper: "We have run our algorithm on 100,000 raster images to recover their vector-graphics representation and 3D popup models." Ecosystem role (Plan2Scene consuming it) not verifiable from these pages. HOWEVER "No 3D artifact" is overstated: the paper and repo explicitly produce "popup 3D models" (Fig. 1/5; abstract: "The vector representation allows 3D model popup"; repo includes a rendering/popup pipeline emitting text files for 3D model generation) — a simple extruded visualization, not a learned 3D output, and no 3D dataset appears to be released (Drive link is vector representations only). LABELS — PARTIAL. "13 junction types" is specifically the WALL junction count: "There are four wall junction types: I-, L-, T-, and X-shaped... Considering orientations, we have in total 13 (= 4+4+4+1) types"; total junction heatmaps are 21 (13 wall + 4 opening + 4 icon-corner): "there are at total 21(= 13 + 4 + 4) different types" (pytorch/utils.py: NUM_WALL_CORNERS=13, NUM_CORNERS=21). Wall segments: confirmed. Openings undifferentiated in geometry: confirmed — "openings (doors or windows)... Door and window symbols are usually indistinguishable, and are modeled as the same 'openings'"; "An opening primitive... does not have any semantics associated at this layer" (a post-processing heuristic later relabels outside-facing openings as windows). Per-pixel room-type labels: confirmed — per-pixel PDF over 12 classes with 11 room types: living-room, kitchen, bedroom, bathroom, restroom, washing-room, balcony, closet, corridor, pipe space, outside. Icon classes: the claim's list is inaccurate — paper: "there are 8 icon types: cooking counter, bathtub, toilet, washing basin, refrigerator, entrance mat, column, or stairs"; pytorch/utils.py labelMap uses bathtub, cooking_counter, toilet, entrance, washing_basin, special, stairs (NUM_ICONS=7). Neither source has "sink" or "closet" as icons (closet is a room type; washing basin is the sink-like class); "special" exists only in the code, "refrigerator/column" only in the paper. AVAILABILITY — CONFIRMED. LICENSE file is "MIT License". README: "To use our trained model, please first download it from Google Drive" (Torch original) and "A PyTorch version is now available under folder pytorch/" with its own Google-Drive-hosted checkpoint per the repo page. Hand-annotated vector ground truth released: "We don't have the permission to share the rasterized images, which are from the LIFULL dataset. Here we only share our vector-graphics annotations" (paper: 870 annotated plans, 770 train / 100 test). LIFULL restriction via Japanese national institute: paper reference [4] points LIFULL HOME'S dataset to nii.ac.jp (National Institute of Informatics IDR, application required). Note: CVF openaccess URLs (paper PDF and abstract HTML) returned HTTP 403 to the fetch tool twice; the PDF was successfully obtained by direct download (PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest) and read in full, so the paper URL itself is valid.
verify.corrections: Icon classes should read (paper): cooking counter, bathtub, toilet, washing basin, refrigerator, entrance mat, column, stairs (8 types); or (released PyTorch code): bathtub, cooking_counter, toilet, entrance, washing_basin, special, stairs (7 icons) — NOT "sink" and NOT "closet" (closet is one of the 11 per-pixel ROOM types: living-room, kitchen, bedroom, bathroom, restroom, washing-room, balcony, closet, corridor, pipe space, outside). "13 junction types" = 13 WALL junction types only (I/L/T/X × orientations); the network regresses 21 junction heatmaps total (13 wall + 4 opening + 4 icon-corner). "No 3D artifact" should be softened to "no learned/textured 3D output or 3D dataset; the pipeline does include a simple extruded 'popup 3D model' visualization (paper Fig. 1/5 and repo popup/rendering code)". Availability otherwise correct as claimed (MIT code, Torch + PyTorch Google Drive weights, 870 hand-annotated vector GT released, LIFULL rasters restricted via Japan's National Institute of Informatics agreement).

verified.pairing: 2D raster plan -> per-pixel room-boundary map (wall, door/window) + room-type map of the same plan; trained on R2V and R3D (Rent3D) annotations. 2D->2D-semantics only.
verified.availability: Original: GPL-3.0, TensorFlow-GPU 1.10.1 / Python 2.7, weights via pretrained/download_links.txt (bit-rotting). TF2DeepFloorplan port: GPL-3.0, TF2.x/Python 3.8, weights on Google Drive (~257MB incl. 37MB TFLite), Docker/Colab/CPU inference supported — trivially runs on a 6GB GPU or CPU.

F4: door and window are COLLAPSED into a single thin 'opening' boundary class — pixel methods cannot distinguish glass from door; room-boundary-guided attention exists precisely because room semantics leak across thin boundaries.

lessons: Sliding-door ground truth exists in exactly one public lineage: vector-CAD symbol datasets. FloorPlanCAD (https://huggingface.co/datasets/Voxel51/FloorPlanCAD) types doors as {single, double, SLIDING} and windows as {window, bay, blind, opening symbol} at line-primitive level, and ArchCAD-400K (https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.22346) scales the approach 26x. No photo/pano/3D dataset types doors at all (ZInD stops at window/door/opening). So F4 symbol conventions must be learned from CAD-vector corpora, and our thin-line glass problem will not be solved by any render-paired dataset off the shelf.

Orientation (F2) ground truth lives only on the 3D side of synthetic designer corpora: 3D-FRONT gives per-instance rotation (https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.09127), SpatialLM gives oriented bboxes over 59 classes (https://arxiv.org/html/2506.07491v2), Structured3D/InteriorGS give 3D boxes. No 2D plan dataset annotates furniture facing. Backwards-learning recipe: render plan-style 2D projections from these designer 3D scenes to mint symbol→facing pairs — the pairing must be manufactured, it is never shipped.

Real same-design 2D↔3D pairs exist at scale in exactly three places, all friction-gated: ZInD (plan + 67K panos of 1,575 real homes; academic-only + written proposal, https://github.com/zillow/zind), LIFULL HOME'S (5.33M listings, plan + room photos of the same unit; NII research application, https://www.nii.ac.jp/dsc/idr/en/lifull/), and tiny curated Rent3D++ (215 units with indoor/outdoor room labels, Google Form, https://3dlg-hcvc.github.io/plan2scene/). These are the honest owner-free benchmark substrate; everything larger is synthetic.

F3 (indoor/outdoor) is supervised today only as ROOM-TYPE vocabulary on the 2D side: Swiss Dwellings separates walls from RAILINGS and types areas incl. balconies under CC BY 4.0 (https://zenodo.org/records/7070952), Rent3D++ labels {outdoor, balcony, terrace}, RPLAN has a balcony channel. Railing-vs-wall as distinct separator classes in Swiss Dwellings is the closest public analog to our glass-facade-as-true-boundary problem — worth mining before building our own annotation schema.

F5 (floor membership of drawn elements) has NO explicit public ground truth anywhere we found. Nearest proxies: per-floor plans of multi-storey real homes in ZInD (panos see through glass to ground-level objects absent from the plan = free negative evidence) and floor-indexed apartments in Swiss Dwellings/MSD. This confirms F5 stays owner-signed in our ledger and is a defensible niche if we ever publish a benchmark.

License gradient matters for a commercial studio: CC BY 4.0 direct-download (Swiss Dwellings, MSD, ResPlan) > CC BY-NC (CubiCasa5K BY-NC-SA 5.5GB zero-friction, FloorPlanCAD BY-NC) > signed-agreement research (Structured3D, 3D-FRONT, Aria Synthetic Environments, RPLAN) > proposal-gated (ZInD, LIFULL) > rights-reserved platform data (SpatialLM/InteriorGS — Kujiale reserves asset rights). NC/agreement sets are fine for internal capability evaluation, but anything whose labels we CODIFY into the product should preferentially come from the CC BY 4.0 tier or our own data.

Symbol conventions are market-specific — Finland (CubiCasa5K), China (FloorPlanCAD/ArchCAD, and all big synthetic corpora derive from Chinese design platforms Kujiale/Alibaba), Japan (LIFULL), Switzerland (Swiss Dwellings), US (ZInD) — and no Thai floor-plan dataset exists in public. Two consequences: (a) FloorPlanCAD's 35-class line-level taxonomy is the right schema TEMPLATE to fork for a Thai symbol codebook; (b) WAFFLE's legend-grounding trick (read the plan's own legend/text to label its symbols, https://tau-vailab.github.io/WAFFLE/) is directly applicable to Thai PDFs, whose BF-style labels our pipeline already reads.

Furnished-ness splits the field: the only fully furnished + fully labeled corpora are synthetic (Structured3D, 3D-FRONT, SpatialLM, InteriorGS, ASE), while the real paired sets are unfurnished (ZInD) or photo-only (LIFULL). Therefore F1/F2 benchmarks must be synthetic-first with a small real photo-verified eval slice (LIFULL/Rent3D++ style), whereas F3/F4/F5 evals can be built on real vector corpora (Swiss Dwellings) plus ZInD W/D/O.

ArchCAD-400K's construction trick — auto-generating labels from CAD layer/block attributes of archived drawings (https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.22346) — transfers to us: when a Thai project ever supplies DXF/DWG alongside PDF, layer names are free semantic ground truth for the PDF's symbols of the same design; that is a zero-annotation-cost paired 2D-symbol↔semantics harvest within our own job flow.

The literature splits on EXACTLY our geometric-vs-semantic fault line: the best pure-geometry reconstructors (HEAT github.com/woodfrog/heat; Floor-SP; MonteFloor) deliberately ship NO door/window/furniture semantics, while every method that attempts semantics reports long-tail collapse — SymPoint (arxiv.org/html/2401.10556v1), SOTA on clean VECTOR input, still scores 0.0 PQ on revolving/rolling doors, 6.8 on bay windows, 39.3 on folding doors vs 83.3 overall. F1 identity on rare symbols is a published open problem, not a defect of our pipeline.

Glass is the hardest class in the field's own tables: FloorplanCAD (floorplancad.github.io) had to make 'curtain wall' an explicit stuff class, and even SymPoint gets only ~20-35 PQ on wall/railing/curtain-wall. Pixel-based methods are worse — DeepFloorplan (github.com/zlzeng/DeepFloorplan) collapses door+window into ONE thin 'opening' class. Our F4 (thin-line sliding glass invisible to thick-stroke extraction) is the known weakest point of the entire lineage; the transferable fix is FloorplanCAD's representation: glass/curtain-wall as a first-class PARALLEL-THIN-LINE vector class annotated ON the wall graph — which matches our manual-glass re-injection into wall segments.

F2 (furniture facing) and F5 (floor membership) have NO method and NO benchmark anywhere in the structural line from Liu 2017 through RoomFormer 2023 — no model predicts object orientation or which drawn elements belong to another floor. Our owner-signed rot ledger is not reinventing existing work; the only orientation signal any dataset carries is implicit (door-swing arcs in door symbols; furniture orientation visible in Structured3D renders). If we want F2 ground truth, we must derive it backwards from 3D artifacts ourselves.

Zeng 2019's published failure cases are literally our failure cases: (a) a large icon misread as a WALL because its strokes resemble wall geometry (= our dimension-label-cluster-as-furniture, F1), and (b) inside/outside region confusion on unusual corridor geometry (= our lounge-vs-terrace, F3) — see openaccess.thecvf.com/content_ICCV_2019/supplemental/Zeng_Deep_Floor_Plan_ICCV_2019_supplemental.pdf. These recur across a decade of methods, i.e., they are structural weaknesses of plan semantics, which strengthens the case for a semantic-truth ledger over model retraining.

Backwards-learning pairs already exist, free, in three tiers: (1) Structured3D (github.com/bertjiazheng/Structured3D) — 3,500 professional designs with plan + 3D planes + photorealistic renders in EMPTY vs FURNISHED configurations of the same rooms: furniture identity (F1), facing-visible-in-render (F2), glazing/balcony visibility (F3/F4) verifiable with zero human labels; (2) Rent3D (cs.toronto.edu/~fidler/projects/rent3D.html) and Rent3D++ via Plan2Scene (github.com/3dlg-hcvc/plan2scene) — real plans + photos ALIGNED to plan positions; (3) FloorNet's 155 RGBD-scanned homes + annotated plans and ZInD's 1,575 real homes (github.com/zillow/zind) with W/D/O + floor plans. An owner-free benchmark can be assembled today from these.

Every mature system in this line converged on a deterministic GLOBAL-CONSISTENCY solver as the reliability step, not a better classifier: Raster-to-Vector's integer programming (openings must lie on walls, loops close), Floor-SP's room-wise shortest-path energy, MonteFloor's MCTS over proposals scored by scene fit (arxiv.org/abs/2103.11161). Transfer: competing semantic reads (desk-vs-cabinet, indoor-vs-outdoor) should be resolved as proposal SELECTION under room-context constraints — the same shape as our placement gate — rather than trusted per-symbol.

3D lifters trust the 2D read blindly: Plan2Scene takes room category, opening positions, and object placement ON FAITH from the plan annotation and only learns appearance from photos; all its reported failures are photo-side (arxiv.org/abs/2106.05375). The industry pattern is 'garbage-in propagates' — validating gating semantics BEFORE the 3D build instead of hoping the 3D stage repairs it.

The field's post-2024 recipe for long-tail symbol identity is machine-proposes/human-signs: DoorDet (arxiv.org/abs/2508.07714) builds door-subtype ground truth via generic detector -> LLM classification of each crop with CONTEXT -> human-in-the-loop verification; and the ASCAAD door study (papers.cumincad.org/data/works/att/ascaad2022_065.pdf) shows swing doors hit 97.7% while some symbols are human-hard — so route by per-class confidence: auto-accept common classes, force sign-off on the known-bad tail (sliding/folding/revolving doors, bay windows, curtain walls).

Indoor/outdoor IS a benchmarkable label today: CubiCasa5K (zenodo.org/record/2613548, CC BY-NC-SA, 5.5GB, no approval) carries 'Outdoor' and 'Railing' as first-class room polygons across 5,000 plans, and Rent3D photo scene-types include outdoor — an F3 regression suite can be built without any client data.

Runnable on our 6GB GPU / CPU today: TF2DeepFloorplan (github.com/zcemycl/TF2DeepFloorplan — TFLite + CPU, weights public), CubiCasa5K PyTorch model (Google Drive weights), RoomFormer (MIT, ETH polybox checkpoints), HEAT inference checkpoints (non-commercial only), SymPoint weights (needs detectron2; trained on 8xA100 but 66ms/drawing inference). Bit-rotted or unreleased: FloorNet and original DeepFloorplan (Python 2.7 / TF1.x), Floor-SP dataset (corporate), MonteFloor (never released), GAT-CADNet (no code). NOTE licenses: HEAT and FloorplanCAD/CubiCasa5K annotations are non-commercial — usable for internal benchmark calibration, not for shipping a trained model commercially without review.

Representation convention worth codifying: every vector-era system represents doors/windows/openings as INTERVALS ATTACHED TO THE WALL GRAPH (R2V opening segments, Plan2Scene wall cuts, ZInD W/D/O boxes on layout walls, RoomFormer door/window polygons on room boundaries) — never as free-floating symbols. ZInD further separates 'opening' (passage, no door) from door and window, and formalizes raw/complete/VISIBLE geometry — the cleanest published vocabulary for our glass-line-as-true-boundary problem, including their own warning that W/D/O labels misalign between adjacent rooms.

General-purpose VLMs are quantitatively worst at exactly our failure list: 33-38% semantic accuracy on CAD floor plans (ArchPlanVQA, ascelibrary.org/doi/10.1061/JCCEE5.CPENG-7571), 0.40-0.55 accuracy counting doors/windows (AECV-Bench, arXiv:2601.04819), and <50% on left/right orientation (3DSRBench, arXiv:2412.07825). F1 identity and F2 facing must stay deterministic/owner-signed; a VLM cannot be the verifier of record.

Input representation dominates VLM accuracy: giving the model the VECTOR (SVG/JSON) alongside or instead of the raster lifts room counting from 0.75 to 0.96 for GPT-4o and label-F1 from 0.70 to 0.88 for open models (arXiv:2511.03478). Our vector-PDF cluster extraction is the right substrate — any future VLM assist should consume per-cluster structured JSON + a cropped view, never the whole-page raster.

The 'backwards' check should be SYMBOLIC, not visual: SceneCritic (arXiv:2604.13035) shows VLM judges of rendered views swing 75%→55% with viewpoint, vary ±19 pts on re-evaluation, and agree with humans only 47-59%, while symbolic scene-graph checks (including back-to-wall and object-pair FACING rules) reach 83-94% human agreement. Render-vs-plan consistency = compare scene graphs / oriented boxes deterministically; renders are for the human's eyes, not the machine judge.

Agentic multi-stage parsing with a structured-graph intermediate and a self-critic beats direct single-call VLM reads by ~15 percentage points, and single-call LLMs hallucinate room adjacencies (arXiv:2604.23970, arXiv:2512.12177). Our gate+ledger+re-inject architecture matches the published best practice; the missing piece they add is a specialist detector (YOLO-class) for doors, not a smarter general model.

Real 2D↔3D paired data for owner-free backwards learning exists today: ZInD (github.com/zillow/zind — 1,524 real homes, plans + 71K localized panoramas + windows/doors/OPENINGS annotations; covers F2 orientation, F3 indoor/outdoor, F4 glass openings), Plan2Scene/Rent3D++ (github.com/3dlg-hcvc/plan2scene — real plans + photos of the same residences), and Structured3D (3,500 CAD houses + 196K renders + furnished/empty pairs for F1/F5). None cover Thai drawing conventions — they calibrate the method, our own signed ledger stays the Thai-symbol ground truth.

For F1 furniture-symbol identity, the proven automation path is panoptic symbol spotting over vector primitives (FloorPlanCAD 15K+ real plans, ArchCAD-400K ~400K; taxonomy already includes bed/wardrobe/tv_cabinet/bedside_cupboard — floorplancad.github.io), where specialist models score high PQ on the same door/window classes general VLMs fail at. A small fine-tuned VLM can also learn plan geometry to 92.5% wall IoU (FloorplanVLM, arXiv:2602.06507) but no published system in the 2024-2026 VLM era addresses F3 indoor-vs-outdoor zoning or F5 floor membership at all — those remain owner-only semantics with no benchmark, i.e., the owner-signed semantic ledger is genuinely novel ground.

Even with perfect structured input and no vision at all, frontier LLMs still violate physical constraints and spatial coherence on layout QA (FloorplanQA, arXiv:2507.07644, ICML 2026) — so post-hoc symbolic validation (our placement/function gates) is required regardless of how good the reader model gets.

ArchDaily is the richest confirmed source of professional plan+photo pairs and has Thai-local volume (Houses-in-Thailand category; 5 project pages machine-verified today: MYJ House, B House, Southwest House, Flow House, Sandwash Apartment), but its ToS bans all robot AND manual scraping without written permission — so the backwards-learning corpus must be a small human-curated few-shot teaching set (personal viewing), with the induced SYMBOL RULES codified into knowledge/ rather than the images stored. (archdaily.com/content/terms-of-use)

Bot-access reality check: Dezeen, Archello, and Hipflat all returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch on 2026-07-06 while ArchDaily and Behance fetched fine — any pipeline assuming automated pair harvesting from architecture media will silently lose 3 of 5 major sources; plan for human-in-browser curation.

For F5 (floor membership), the underused artifact is the SECTION drawing: multi-storey ArchDaily houses publish 3-4 sections alongside stacked plans (B House: 4 sections; MYJ House: 2), and a section states unambiguously which drawn element sits on which slab — a machine-checkable complement to the owner-only floor-membership call. (archdaily.com/947664, archdaily.com/1009563)

For F1/F2, the highest-yield genre is the '3D floor plan' visualization portfolio (Behance, 10k+ projects): the author re-states their own 2D plan as a pixel-aligned top-down 3D render, so every furniture symbol maps to an identified, oriented 3D model — a direct symbol→identity+facing rosetta with no photogrammetry needed. (behance.net/gallery/131037153, behance.net/search/projects/3d%20floor%20plan)

Same-author AXONOMETRIC/isometric drawings on project pages (Southwest House, Flow House) are the cheapest single-image bridge between plan symbols and 3D form — treat 'has axo' as a selection criterion when curating benchmark pairs. (archdaily.com/1018390, archdaily.com/1023589)

Thai condo marketing unit plans systematically LIE about scale: the hawook guide documents that furniture symbols are scaled down and walls drawn thinner for marketing effect — so backwards-learning from developer plans should harvest IDENTITY and FACING (F1/F2) but never dimensions; dimension truth stays with the deterministic extractor. (hawook.com/understanding-condo-plan-...)

For F3/F4, Matterport schematic floor plans are the only perfectly-registered 2D<->3D pairs by construction (the plan is generated from the scan, RICS-standard, SVG = parseable vectors): the tour shows the real glass boundary and indoor/outdoor state that the plan then symbolizes. Two uses: (a) study per-listing pairs; (b) scan the studio's own completed projects to legally mint ground-truth pairs. (matterport.com/schematic-floor-plans)

Micro-apartment roundups (ArchDaily 'Under 30m2', 13 projects, 6+ in-page pairs) are the densest curation unit for the desk-vs-cabinet error class: transformable furniture (fold-down beds, sliding storage walls) has maximally ambiguous plan symbols that the paired photos resolve. (archdaily.com/934616)

ArchDaily DOES have a plan-image search at scale (search/images with an image_type/drawings facet, plus tag/floor-plans), and every drawing links back to its parent project — technically a pair-index — but it is a JS-rendered SPA and covered by the same no-scrape ToS, so it serves as a human browsing accelerator, not an API. (archdaily.com/search/us/images/image_type/drawings)

The domain-matched at-scale channel for the studio's segment is Thai condo portals (Hipflat/DDproperty: thousands of projects pairing unit-type plans with show-unit photos) — the same unit type repeats across many listings, giving natural redundancy for convention-mining, but pages are bot-blocked and unlicensed, so mine them by reading and codifying rules, not by copying images. (hipflat.com/thailand-projects/condo, ddproperty.com/en/condo-directory)

Government free-plan programs are the only Thai source that is simultaneously large, paired, and legally safe for internal ML study: BMA HomeSmile alone gives 100+ designs where every design ships a floor-plan image AND a 3D perspective of the same house in one free .rar (yotathai.com/yotanews/plan3d-homesmile2), and DPT/GHB/NHA/DEDE add permit-grade full sets — all published explicitly for unrestricted public use, unlike developer/review content.

Full permit sets, not the plan sheet, carry the F4 answer: Thai construction sets pair every thin-line opening with a door/window SCHEDULE code (ป./น.) plus elevations, so a sliding glass door invisible to thick-stroke wall extraction is named explicitly elsewhere in the same PDF (DPT house_ready_*.pdf sets; ASA 2554 standard codifies the symbols, incl. arrow=sliding-direction, no-arrow=fixed per TOSTEM explainer). Backwards-learning should join plan geometry to schedule text, and the studio should codify symbols from the ASA standard rather than re-derive them per plan.

Exterior perspectives (the government pairs) teach F1/F3/F5 but are weak for F2 (furniture facing); real facing ground truth lives in show-unit 360 tours and review-site photo walkthroughs paired with the same unit type's marketing plan (thinkofliving 'รีวิวตึกเสร็จ/พาชมห้องตัวอย่าง' series, LH '360 View Image & 3D Floor Plan', home.co.th/virtual, Sansiri virtual hub). These are copyrighted and anti-bot (thinkofliving/home.co.th/fazwaz all return 403 to automated fetch) — use them as manual view-and-annotate benchmarks, never scrape.

Thai plans come in two symbol dialects and a benchmark needs both: marketing unit plans (developer sites, reviews, builder catalogs — furnished symbols, Thai room labels like ระเบียง/ห้องนั่งเล่น that directly encode F3/F5 semantics) vs ASA-coded permit sets (schedule codes, hatches). Builder catalogs (Seacon 200+, PD House 200+, verified template: seacon.co.th/home/สุดคุ้ม-3/) give the marketing dialect at bulk scale in a uniform, scriptable page template.

DEDE's 'บ้านดีดี' set (12 designs × 24 plot-orientation options with matched docs, yotathai.com/yotanews/plan-baan-dede) is a ready-made orientation-perturbation corpus: the same plan documented facing every cardinal direction — directly usable to test whether the reader's F2/orientation decisions are invariant to plan rotation instead of memorized.

F5 supervision is cheap from any 2-storey free-plan set: Thai sets always separate แปลนชั้นล่าง/แปลนชั้นบน plus a roof plan, and the single exterior perspective shows which drawn elements (carport, terrace, garden trees) are ground-level — aligning perspective content to the correct storey sheet yields labeled 'drawn-here-but-belongs-below' examples without an owner in the loop.

Access pattern observed across ~20 fetches: government subsites and mirrors (yotathai, naibann, kapook, checkraka, ghbank, seacon, apthai) fetch cleanly; the highest-value REAL-photo pairings (thinkofliving, home.co.th, fazwaz, thaiwatsadu) are uniformly 403 to bots — plan the benchmark as (a) automated ingestion of government pairs + builder catalogs, (b) a small human-curated set from review sites for the semantic classes F2/F3/F4 that only real photos resolve.

Door OPERATION is deterministically encoded in stroke geometry, per both standards and textbook: quarter-circle arc = hinged (swing side = arc side), two offset parallel thin rectangles in a wall gap = sliding, nested lines = pocket, zigzag/peaks = folding. Ching states plans show 'the type of door operation—whether a door swings, slides, or folds open' (archive.org 6th ed.); ISO 7519:2025 has normative clauses 6.2.2 'Door swings' and 6.6 'Arrow symbols'. A thin parallel-line pair in a wall gap is a SLIDING (usually glass) door, not absent wall — fixes F4's invisible sliding glass door with a rule, not a human.

Glass is drawn THIN by norm, not by accident, and lives on its own layer family: ASA 2554 assigns full-height glass walls to A-GLAZ-FULL at pen 0.25 (vs 0.35-0.5+ for cut walls), AIA/NCS defines A-GLAZ-FULL/-PRHT/-SILL, and practitioner guides describe glass partitions as 'thin single or double lines' with optional GL/diamond markers. Codifiable F4 rule: run a second thin-stroke pass; any thin line chain that closes a room boundary or spans a wall gap is a glazing candidate; if the source PDF preserves DWG layer names or pen widths, 0.25mm-class strokes between wall ends ARE the room's true boundary.

Floor MEMBERSHIP (F5) has explicit linework semantics: dashed thin lines = objects above or below the plan cut (ASA 2554 p.8-8 verbatim; Ching: 'dashed lines indicate major architectural features that occur above the plane of the plan cut'); ISO 7519 uses long-dashed-dotted (04.2) for above-ground projections like balconies and dashed (02.2) for below-ground; NCS has A-FLOR-OVHD. Inverse rule for the garden-tree trap: solid-linework vegetation on an upper-floor sheet that sits OUTSIDE the glass boundary and on landscape-style symbols (canopy circle + trunk dot, drawn at mature canopy size per Draftscapes) belongs to grade (NCS discipline L-PLNT-TREE), while on-structure planters are A-FURN-PLNT — the ground-vs-planter question the owner had to answer manually is a layer/discipline distinction in the standards.

FACING (F2) is conventionally implied by symbol asymmetry, and only for some classes: bed faces away from the headboard/pillow end (thin rectangle at one short end); sofa/armchair face away from the backrest strip ('thinner rectangle along the back edge' — Cedreo/PlanSnapper); armchairs are 'often shown angled toward a conversation area' (aim = shared focal); desk sitting side = the chair square/circle; wall-mounted TV face = the thin line side away from the wall. Build facing extraction ONLY for asymmetric symbols and keep symmetric ones (plain rectangles) in the owner-review lane — the convention itself has no facing for them.

Symbol conventions are jurisdiction- and era-versioned, so the symbol->meaning table needs metadata, and legends outrank the table: AS 1100.301's own preface documents Australia REVERTING its hinged door/window convention after 2008 (and NZ differing), and ISO 7519 4.1.2 makes a referenced symbols legend normative. Deterministic pipeline order: parse the sheet's own legend first; fall back to the jurisdictional default table only for symbols the legend omits; both Board&Vellum and Quora-tier practitioner sources repeat 'when in doubt, consult the plan legend'.

INDOOR vs OUTDOOR (F3) is signaled by a bundle, not one mark: outdoor decks/patios get surface-material hatching ('rectangle with a grid or line pattern indicating the surface material' — Cedreo) and/or dashed outlines + text labels outside the main wall line (BigRentz), while interior floors at 1:100 are typically unhatched. Critically, F3 and F4 interact: a 'terrace-looking' hatched zone whose boundary is closed by a thin glazing line is an interior glazed room — so the indoor/outdoor classifier must consume the thin-line glazing extraction, plus zone label text (Thai: ระเบียง/เฉลียง vs ห้องนั่งเล่น) as the primary human-authored signal.

Annotation clusters have their own closed symbol vocabulary, which fixes the dimension-label-misread-as-furniture failure (F1): door/window tags are small geometric frames (circle/hexagon in Thai practice, per dsignsomething; 'D/ป' and 'W/น' + number), room IDs are boxed text, grid callouts are circles on chain lines, section markers have arrows+sheet numbers (Archtoolbox). A pre-filter that recognizes and REMOVES the annotation vocabulary (tag frames, dimension strings, leaders, north arrows, revision clouds) before furniture clustering eliminates that false-positive class deterministically — and the tags then become ground truth links into door/window schedules for identity and glass type.

An owner-free benchmark for identity+facing can be assembled from free block/drawing libraries: CAD-blocks.net / Bibliocad (120k+ blocks) supply canonical labeled DWG plan symbols per class — compose them into synthetic vector plans to get perfect identity/orientation ground truth for the reader; Dimensions.com pairs the SAME object as 2D plan drawing (.DWG/.SVG) and 3D model (.SKP/.OBJ/.3DM) with verified dimensions, giving per-object 2D-symbol->3D-orientation alignment without any owner labeling. This is the cheap 'learn backwards' loop for F1/F2 while real 2D+3D project pairs are scarcer.

For Thai residential PDFs specifically, the ASA มาตรฐานการเขียนแบบก่อสร้าง 2554 (free 270-page PDF, text-extractable) is the single highest-value codification source: it is the standard Thai offices were taught to follow, it maps every relevant semantic class (glass wall, curtain wall, built-in vs loose furniture, plants/pots, door swing, openings-dashed) to explicit layer names, pen widths and linetypes, includes a มอก.(TIS)-vs-NCS line-width concordance and a Thai-English abbreviation table — worth distilling into knowledge/ as the backbone of the symbol->meaning rule set (ingest via _inbox flow; the PDF is already downloaded in this session's tool-results).

F1 is the industry-wide unsolved layer, stated in vendors' own words: RoomSketcher AI Convert does walls/doors/windows only and answers 'Does it convert furniture?' with 'Not yet, but stay tuned!' despite 50k+ training plans (roomsketcher.com/features/ai-convert); Planner 5D limits itself to 'basic furniture like beds, bathrooms, tables' and 'might not identify... a refrigerator' (support.planner5d.com); Coohom recognizes only bed/sofa/dining-table/toilet (coohom.com helpcenter). A closed-set furniture vocabulary + REVIEW for everything else matches industry state of the art — full-open furniture identity is beyond every shipping product.

Our exact failure modes are codified industry failure classes: Coohom's CAD prep instructions order users to DELETE 'various types of dimensions', 'tree', 'car', 'furniture', 'decorative moldings' before recognition (coohom.com/helpcenter/requirements-and-faq-for-uploading-cad-floor-plan-files) — i.e., dimension-label clusters misread as geometry (our F1 label-cluster case) and entourage trees (our F5 garden-trees case) are so unsolvable the market leader makes the HUMAN pre-delete them. Treating dims/trees/entourage as a pre-classified 'annotation/entourage' stratum, not candidate furniture, is the industry-validated move.

Symbol conventions worth hard-coding exist and are published: door = rectangle + arc where 'arcs represent the direction' (door swing = deterministic F2 for doors), window = 3-4 parallel thin lines, sliding door = 'staggered drawing method of 2/3/4 fans', walls = double lines 50-400mm (Coohom helpcenter). Our recurring invisible thin-line sliding glass door (F4) has a known line-count/stagger signature — a targeted thin-line detector keyed to these conventions can flag 'possible opening' for owner sign-off even when the thick-stroke wall extractor sees nothing.

Even HUMAN professional redrawers cannot extract F1/F4 from linework alone: HomeByMe's draw-for-you service asks customers to annotate 'room names and window types' up front (home.by.me/en/services/floorplan-drawing-service), and CubiCasa's whole change-request taxonomy is room labels + window/door TYPES + fixed-furniture add/remove + wall add/suppress (help.cubi.casa change-requests). This is information missing from the drawing, not a vision deficit — validating the owner-signed semantic ledger as the correct architecture rather than a stopgap.

Every '24-hour AI' vendor is secretly human-in-the-loop: getfloorplan has 'a Quality Assurance team checks every AI floor plan' (futurepedia/getfloorplan sources); Planner 5D recognition takes '10 minutes to 24 hours' and low-rated results go 'for a second review'; CubiCasa ships in 24h then runs email-based change requests. Nobody ships zero-touch; the competitive variable is correction COST (CubiCasa's 'half a dozen emails' vs our goal of one signed click) — 'machine makes owner corrections cheap' is exactly where the market differentiates.

Verifier UX gap confirmed in the field: a CubiCasa reviewer's core grievance is 'the software doesn't retain the video... for you to review and compare to the output' (Capterra reviews) — the missing evidence-overlay is a known pain, so wiring raster_overlay.py as the required pre-owner artifact directly implements what paying users of the market leader ask for.

F3/F5 errors ship in production at the market leader: 'a random exterior fence being included in GLA floorspace' (CubiCasa Capterra review) is indoor/outdoor + membership misclassification surviving both AI and vendor QA — our F3/F5 owner-only classification is not over-caution; the best-funded pipeline with human QA still leaks these.

No vendor publishes semantic accuracy — CubiCasa's 95-97% is dimensional scan accuracy, floor-plan.ai's '99.5% conversion accuracy' has no methodology or examples, magicplan publishes no number at all. An F1-F5 semantic benchmark scored against human-adjudicated ground truth would measure something the industry demonstrably does not measure — and vendor showcase pairs (getfloorplan's 2D→furnished-3D+tour deliverables at $35/plan, CubiCasa 2D/3D pairs) are purchasable human-verified pairs: for ~$1k one could commission ~30 generic plans through such services and harvest QA-passed semantic interpretations as benchmark labels (privacy-safe if seeded with public/synthetic plans, never client plans).

One immediately usable free asset: CubiCasa5K (github.com/CubiCasa/CubiCasa5k, zenodo.org/record/2613548) — 5,000 real plans with SVG polygon ground truth across 80+ categories separating room classes / furniture-fixture icons / structure. It directly supports learning-backwards for F1 (icon identity vs annotation) and partially F3 (room-type taxonomy), with the caveat that conventions are Finnish; validate symbol transfer against Thai plans before trusting it as a convention codex.

Vector interchange destroys semantics industry-wide: Floorplanner's DXF export turns 'text labels... into a mass of little lines' and drops furniture entirely (GetApp/Trustpilot reviews) — the outlined-text-no-OCR problem our pipeline hits is endemic to the format, so identity must be recovered from geometry+context+human signature, never expected from the vector file itself.
